identity.title: The Geometry of Categorical and Hierarchical Concepts in Large Language Models

problem.claim: Formalize how categorical and hierarchical concepts are represented geometrically in LLM representation spaces.

gap.claim: Prior formalization addressed binary concepts with natural contrasts, leaving features without natural contrasts and broader categorical or hierarchical structure less formalized.

contributions.claim: Extends the linear representation hypothesis by representing features such as is_animal as vectors.
Formalizes categorical concepts as polytopes and proves a relationship between conceptual hierarchy and representation geometry.
Applies the formalization to hierarchically related concepts in Gemma and LLaMA-3 using WordNet data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state an extension from linear directions for contrasted binary concepts to vector representations for features, enabling a polytope-based treatment of categorical concepts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validating their theoretical results on Gemma and LLaMA-3.
The authors report estimating representations for more than 900 hierarchically related concepts using WordNet data.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper situates its work in the linear representation hypothesis, where semantic concepts are encoded as linear directions.
Existing formalization is described for binary concepts with natural contrasts.
The authors extend the formalization to vectors for features lacking natural contrasts and represent categorical concepts as polytopes.
They state a hierarchy–geometry relationship and report validation on Gemma and LLaMA-3 across 900+ WordNet-linked concepts.

source_observation.claim: The abstract introduces a representational extension, derives a geometric consequence, and then reports model-level validation over a large hierarchy of concepts.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can align a formal generalization with its structural implication and an explicitly scoped validation target.
lessons.application: When presenting a representation proposal, state the limitation it addresses, the mathematical object it enables, the structural claim derived from it, and the models or data used to assess that claim.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no formal extension, structural consequence, or concrete validation scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proved hierarchy–geometry relationship, validation procedure, or quantitative validation results.
It does not identify which 900+ concepts or how their representations were estimated.
